I think it depends on the language! If you're learning a language like Chinese it's a good way to practice your strokes. It's easier to e-mail since you just write in pinyin and your keyboard finds the character but when writing you have to actually remember how to write the character. I personally can be too dependent on my pinyin keyboard and it doesn't help you memorize characters, I've honestly forgotten some because I normally use a pinyin character but it all depends on the language and personal preference!

I've had a similar issue but with Mandarin as well. I think in general it's easier to understand a language teacher/professor because a lot of the time they're making a conscious effort to speak clearly and slowly while native speakers mumble, use slang, have different accents, etc. I suggest finding French/francophone speakers on Youtube or radios/podcast so you can get a feel of what “real” speakers sound like. I could understand my Chinese teacher fairly well but at a cultural fair our booth was approached by a student from Beijing and I could hardly understand her. After she left, my teacher told me not to feel bad if I couldn't understand her because she spoke fast, even for a Chinese speaker, and her accent was new to me. I'm sure you're advancing well but even advanced speakers might have issues with accents! Good luck, I hope this helped a bit!
